# vm-image-admission Specification

<!-- Generated by Prism from prism/spec.json. Change the app through your agent with /prism, not by editing this file. -->

## Purpose

VM image admission: Decide, as an XACML policy decision, whether a VM disk image pulled as an OCI artifact is admitted to a cluster, from its signature, whether its bytes match its digest, its architecture, where it was pulled from, whether the site is air-gapped and whether the verifier answered.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Never permit when signature is not verified

The app SHALL NOT answer `permit` when signature is not verified, because no unverified image ever runs.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-001, theorem `inv001Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-001 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `missing match amd64 mirror connected ok` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `permit`
- **AND** the app answers `deny`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: Never permit when digest is mismatch

The app SHALL NOT answer `permit` when digest is mismatch, because no image whose bytes do not match its digest ever runs.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-002, theorem `inv002Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-002 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `verified mismatch amd64 mirror connected ok` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `permit`
- **AND** the app answers `deny`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: Never permit when site is airgapped and source is upstream

The app SHALL NOT answer `permit` when site is airgapped and source is upstream, because an air-gapped cluster never runs an upstream pull.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-003, theorem `inv003Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-003 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `verified match amd64 upstream airgapped ok` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `permit`
- **AND** the app answers `deny`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: Always indeterminate when verifier is error

The app SHALL answer `indeterminate` when verifier is error, because a verifier error never becomes a permit.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-004, theorem `inv004Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-004 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `verified match amd64 mirror connected error` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `indeterminate`
- **AND** the app answers `indeterminate`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: REQ-001 indeterminate when verifier is error

The app SHALL answer `indeterminate` when verifier is error, because fail closed: a verifier error is not a decision.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule1`).

#### Scenario: REQ-001 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `verified match amd64 mirror connected error` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `indeterminate`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: REQ-002 deny when digest is mismatch

The app SHALL answer `deny` when digest is mismatch and no earlier rule matches, because content addressing: bytes that do not hash to their name are not that image.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule2`).

#### Scenario: REQ-002 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `verified mismatch amd64 mirror connected ok` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `deny`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: REQ-003 deny when signature is not verified

The app SHALL answer `deny` when signature is not verified and no earlier rule matches, because ContainerCraft/kmi: images are Cosign-signed, and an unsigned or badly signed image is refused.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule3`).

#### Scenario: REQ-003 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `missing match amd64 mirror connected ok` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `deny`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: REQ-004 deny when site is airgapped and source is upstream

The app SHALL answer `deny` when site is airgapped and source is upstream and no earlier rule matches, because an air-gapped site pulls only from its own mirror.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule4`).

#### Scenario: REQ-004 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `verified match amd64 upstream airgapped ok` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `deny`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: REQ-005 not-applicable when arch is other

The app SHALL answer `not-applicable` when arch is other and no earlier rule matches, because kmi publishes multi-arch amd64 and arm64 images only.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule5`).

#### Scenario: REQ-005 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `verified match other mirror connected ok` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `not-applicable`, decided by REQ-005

### Requirement: Otherwise permit

The app SHALL answer `permit` when no rule matches, because a verified, matching image of a supported architecture from an allowed source runs.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: No rule matches

- **WHEN** the request is `verified match amd64 mirror airgapped ok` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `permit`

### Requirement: The first matching rule decides

The app SHALL try REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005 in that order, and the first rule that matches SHALL decide.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: Two rules match

- **WHEN** the request is `verified match amd64 upstream airgapped error`
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `indeterminate`, decided by REQ-001, the earlier rule

### Requirement: Request and answers

The app SHALL read one request as one line of 6 fields separated by single spaces, in this order, and SHALL answer exactly one of `permit`, `deny`, `not-applicable`, `indeterminate`, or `invalid` for anything else.

| Field | Accepts | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `signature` | `verified`, `missing`, `invalid` | the Cosign signature check on the image |
| `digest` | `match`, `mismatch` | whether the pulled bytes hash to the digest the reference names |
| `arch` | `amd64`, `arm64`, `other` | the image architecture |
| `source` | `mirror`, `upstream` | pulled from the site's own mirror or from an upstream registry |
| `site` | `airgapped`, `connected` | whether the cluster is disconnected |
| `verifier` | `ok`, `error` | whether the signature verifier answered |

| Answer | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `permit` | the image may run |
| `deny` | the image is refused |
| `not-applicable` | the architecture is one this platform does not run, so no policy applies |
| `indeterminate` | the verifier failed, so no decision is made and nothing runs |
| `invalid` | the request is malformed |

Verified: reading a request is tested, not proved.

#### Scenario: A malformed request is invalid

- **WHEN** the request is not 6 fields in this order
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `invalid`

## Out of scope

- It does not verify signatures itself; it decides from the verifier's result.
- Which keys are trusted is the cluster's policy and outside it.

## Examples

- `verified match amd64 mirror airgapped ok` gives `permit`
- `verified match arm64 upstream connected ok` gives `permit`
- `verified match amd64 upstream airgapped ok` gives `deny`
- `missing match amd64 mirror connected ok` gives `deny`
- `verified mismatch amd64 mirror connected ok` gives `deny`
- `verified match other mirror connected ok` gives `not-applicable`
- `verified match amd64 mirror connected error` gives `indeterminate`

## What is proved and what is tested

Lean proves each property marked proved above, for every request that decodes, with no exceptions and no sampling. The proof is about `judge`, the function the WebAssembly guest runs, because both come from the same model.

The parsing of requests is tested, not proved: the acceptance vectors in the app replay through the built guest, including malformed and oversized requests.

Nothing here says the rules are the right rules. That is the part only you can judge.
